speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To determine the cause of your respiratory distress and the nature of this mass, have you noticed any pain, bloating, or changes in your bowel or bladder habits recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Carcinoma causing Malignant Ascites and Pleural Effusion.

Given your age, lack of prior pregnancies, and the combination of a large ovarian mass with shortness of breath and rapid abdominal distension, this is highly suggestive of advanced ovarian cancer with associated fluid accumulation. I need to confirm the extent of this spread and the nature of the fluid.

REQUEST TEST: CA-125, CT Abdomen and Pelvis with contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: CT Abdomen/Pelvis slices showing the mass and ascites.
